topic: Happy customers do not leave reviews unprompted. Asking is the entire mechanism.

slides.subtitle: (nobody asked them to)
slides.scene: A tidy finished utility room with new copper pipework, warm evening light through a small window, a set of clean tools packed into an open bag on the floor ready to leave. All vehicles and buildings in shot have COMPLETELY BLANK panels and surfaces with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind. No signage anywhere in the scene. There is NO text, no words and no labels anywhere in the image.

caption:
The job went well. They said thanks, paid on time, and you never heard from them again.

That customer would have left you a review. They just were not asked, and nobody wakes up wanting to write one.

This is the cheapest thing on the whole list and it is the one that never happens, because asking has to occur a day or two after the job, on a day when you are already on the next one.

And the ones you do have are old. A review from two years ago does not tell somebody what you are like now, and search results notice.

Every job you finish is a review you did not collect. That is not a marketing problem, it is a timing problem, and timing is exactly the sort of thing that can be handled without you.

If you want to see what that looks like on your own numbers, book a twenty minute walkthrough at scaileai.com.
